---
title: "Examples"
---

The package ships three example models from CmdStanR, with their data: `logistic`, a logistic regression, and `schools` and `schools_ncp`, the eight schools hierarchical model in its centered and non-centered forms. The repository's `examples/` directory has the small programs used in these docs.

## Bundled models

`cmdstanr_example()` compiles an example, fits it with its bundled data, and returns the fit. The first argument names the example, and the second the method: `sample` (the default), `optimize`, `laplace`, `variational`, `pathfinder`, or `diagnose`. Other arguments are passed to the method. The executable is built in the directory set by the `cmdstanphp_example_dir` option, or in `cmdstanphp-examples` under the system temporary directory. `print_example_program()` prints the Stan program.

```php
CmdStan\print_example_program('schools_ncp');

$fit = CmdStan\cmdstanr_example('schools_ncp', seed: 123, show_messages: false);
print_r($fit->summary(['mu', 'tau'], measures: ['mean', 'sd', 'rhat', 'ess_bulk']));
print_r($fit->diagnosticWarnings());
```

```text
data {
  int<lower=1> J;
  vector<lower=0>[J] sigma;
  vector[J] y;
}
parameters {
  real mu;
  real<lower=0> tau;
  vector[J] theta_raw;
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[J] theta = mu + tau * theta_raw;
}
model {
  target += normal_lpdf(tau | 0, 10);
  target += normal_lpdf(mu | 0, 10);
  target += normal_lpdf(theta_raw | 0, 1);
  target += normal_lpdf(y | theta, sigma);
}
Array

```

The centered form, `schools`, samples the same posterior with `theta` as a parameter. With the same seed it produces divergent transitions in every chain:

```php
$fit = CmdStan\cmdstanr_example('schools', seed: 123, show_messages: false);
print_r($fit->diagnosticWarnings());
```

```text
Array
(
    [0] => Chain 1: 73 divergent transitions.
    [1] => Chain 2: 74 divergent transitions.
    [2] => Chain 2: E-BFMI below 0.3.
    [3] => Chain 3: 25 divergent transitions.
    [4] => Chain 4: 8 divergent transitions.
)
```

The [MCMC guide](mcmc.qmd#check-convergence) explains these warnings. The outputs above are from CmdStan 2.40.0 on macOS. Other platforms and CmdStan versions give different draws for the same seed.

## Programs in the repository

The `examples/` directory of the [repository](https://github.com/phpstats/CmdStanPHP/tree/main/examples) holds:

- `bernoulli.stan` and `bernoulli.php`, the model from [Getting started](getting-started.qmd) and a script that samples it. Run `php examples/bernoulli.php` from a clone of the repository after `composer install`.
- `generated.stan`, the Bernoulli model with a posterior prediction, used in [Generated quantities](generated-quantities.qmd).
- `normal.stan`, a one-parameter normal model, used in [Log density and model methods](log-density.qmd).
